Guidance on the orderly cycle
This part of the manual describes the plain rules

Companion Animal Travel Desk Routine Handling

This section sets the standard method for receiving, reviewing, and recording companion animal travel requests so that service is careful, consistent, and centered on animal welfare. Staff must greet each traveler with calm language, confirm the journey details already provided, and keep the exchange concise so the passenger understands the next step without confusion. Where a welfare review is needed, the desk must pass the file to the welfare coordinator without delay and must not promise approval before the review is complete. The travel plan must account for the species, temperament, carrier condition, and comfort needs of the animal, and any sign of distress, unsafe containment, or unsuitable weather exposure must be escalated at once through the proper internal channel.

All guidance given to passengers must be plain, kind, and actionable. Staff should avoid technical terms when simpler wording will do, and should explain only what the passenger needs to do next. If documents are incomplete, the desk must state the missing item directly and must not create exceptions without approval. When a traveler arrives with a pet such as Winnie, the desk must verify the animal's readiness for transport, note any special care concerns, and ensure the owner understands the boarding and transfer process. If more than one department is involved, the desk must keep the record aligned so that no instruction conflicts with another.

Records must be entered promptly and reviewed for accuracy before the case is closed. Any correction to identity, carrier type, route suitability, or welfare note must be written in the file and shared with the relevant team through the approved workflow. Staff must not give casual assurances that are not supported by the record, and they must preserve a respectful tone even when the request cannot be accepted as first presented. This is especially important when the passenger is anxious or the animal appears unsettled, because steady communication reduces risk and helps maintain trust in Aurelia Skyways service.

Questions that cannot be resolved at the desk must be referred to the senior coordinator or the welfare coordinator, as appropriate. For any unresolved concern, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk supervisor for direction.
